errors.text: The hypothesis places the decisive chemical ordering primarily in B2 domains, whereas the target mechanism is enhanced L12 ordering in FCC domains approaching Ni3Al stoichiometry.
It gives an incorrect embrittlement window of roughly 400-600°C and omits the key 600°C ductility minimum and 750°C recovery; the target boundary is approximately 550-750°C.

Phase-boundary morphology is treated only as a passive accommodation response rather than identifying jagged B2/FCC boundary tips as stress concentrators that cooperate with planar slip to initiate instability.

Recovery is partly attributed to thermal activation during deformation, which is not an adequate explanation if specimens are aged at different temperatures and subsequently tested under the same conditions; the target recovery instead involves reduced ordering and ductile transition zones along phase boundaries.

The proposed experiment does not directly test for crack initiation and dislocation pile-ups at jagged phase-boundary tips or independently establish the absence of grain-boundary impurity segregation.
